model: Cube & Rail IP Meter (Ethernet, Modbus TCP)
applies_to: V2 Ethernet versions of the Cube 350I, Cube 350V, Cube 400I and Cube 400V (label 'IP.Ver: V2') and the Rail 350V, per manual revision 1.07p (December 2013).
summary: The Cube and Rail IP meters are Northern Design three-phase meters with a built-in Ethernet port and a Modbus TCP server on port 502. The manual recommends polling the read-only amalgamated data table, which packs energy, volts, amps, power, power factor, demand and the scale exponents into one block of integers. Energy counters are also in a writable 32-bit table.

addressing.note: Tables print a 0-based data address next to the Modicon register number (7680 = 47681). The data address is what goes on the wire: request 7680 to read 47681.

source.title: Cube & Rail IP Meter - Ethernet System Meter Installation and Operation Manual
source.pages: p. 7 (models); pp. 72-74 (Modbus TCP, scaling, energy registers); pp. 81-82 (Appendix A4, Table 30)

notes: Northern Design does not host this manual publicly; the link is a copy on a distributor's file host (the same host used for the Cube 350 and multicube manuals).
32-bit values: every energy row is printed as a High Word at the lower address followed by the Low Word, so ABCD.

Instantaneous values are signed integers of the displayed digits. Real value = raw x 10^(K-3) with K = Ki (7733), Kvp (7734), Kvl (7735) or Kp (7736); demand power rows use Kp + 1. These rows are listed with scale 1 and no unit. Frequency (500 = 50.00), power factor (1000 = 1.000) have fixed printed scales.
Energy counts: kWh = raw x 10^(Ke-6) and Wh = raw x 10^(Ke-3). The manual's formula names register 40516, but its worked example shows the 40515-40516 pair is meant. Ke is at 513 and also at 7737.
The data type of the Ki/Kvp/Kvl/Kp/Ke registers is not printed; they are small positive exponents (the example gives 1 to 4), listed as UINT16.
Row 7684 is printed only as 'Kvarh' without saying inductive or capacitive.
Left out: amalgamated data table 2 (5632-5672). Several of its rows are marked Read/Write while the table note says the whole table is read only, and most rows give no data format.
The TCP server supports functions 3, 4 and 6 only (no function 16).

integration.summary: Connect to port 502 and read the amalgamated table 7680-7737 with function 03 (split into requests your client accepts). Read the scale exponents at 7733-7737 first, then apply raw x 10^(K-3) to each instantaneous value and 10^(Ke-6) to the energy counts.
integration.enable: The manual describes no enable step: the Modbus TCP server answers on port 502 at the meter's IP address. By default the meter takes its IP settings from DHCP and falls back to 192.168.1.127 if none is found; the address can also be set on the front panel or the Network Settings web page.
quirks: The amalgamated tables refresh once per second; polling faster gains nothing.
Scale registers are exponents offset by 3 (raw x 10^(K-3)), not plain multipliers.
Only functions 3, 4 and 6 are implemented; clients that write with function 16 will be refused.
setup: Port 502. The meter uses DHCP by default (fallback 192.168.1.127, mask 255.255.255.0); a static address can be set on the front panel or the Network Settings web page.
The manual covers V2 IP meters only; check the rear label for 'IP.Ver: V2'.
gotchas: The energy counters at 514-529 are writable; a stray write changes the stored totals.
The amalgamated tables are read only; write energy presets through the 512-529 block instead.

address_note: address = 0-based Modbus wire (PDU) address; documented = as printed in the source.
